items.labelEn: Caesium-133 hyperfine transition frequency (defines the second)
items.labelFr: Fréquence de la transition hyperfine du césium 133 (définit la seconde)
items.conditions: Exact by definition (SI 2019); unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition of the caesium-133 atom.
items.locator: Table 1 (seven defining constants), PDF p. 14; definition of the second, §2.3.1, PDF p. 16
items.quote: The effect of this definition is that the second is equal to the duration of 9 192 631 770 periods
items.confidenceNotes: Exact value. Cross-checked on src-bipm-second-page.

items.labelEn: One period of the caesium-133 reference radiation
items.labelFr: Une période du rayonnement de référence du césium 133
items.conditions: Derived from the exact SI definition.
items.quote: the second is equal to the duration of 9 192 631 770 periods
items.confidenceNotes: Exact up to floating-point rounding.

items.labelEn: Speed of light in vacuum
items.labelFr: Vitesse de la lumière dans le vide
items.conditions: Exact by definition (defining constant of the SI).
items.locator: Table 1, PDF p. 14; §2.3.1 definition of the metre, PDF p. 16
items.quote: This definition implies the exact relation c = 299 792 458 m s−1.
items.confidenceNotes: Also NIST CODATA 2022: '299 792 458 m s-1', uncertainty '(exact)' (src-nist-codata-c).

items.labelEn: Distance travelled by light in vacuum in 1 ns
items.labelFr: Distance parcourue par la lumière dans le vide en 1 ns
items.conditions: Vacuum. In optical fibre or copper, propagation is slower (group index not sourced here, see excluded).
items.calculation: d = c x 1e-9 s = 299 792 458 m/s x 1e-9 s; input: speed-of-light-vacuum
items.quote: This definition implies the exact relation c = 299 792 458 m s−1.
items.confidenceNotes: Exact.

items.labelEn: Astronomical unit
items.labelFr: Unité astronomique
items.conditions: Conventional exact length (IAU 2012 Resolution B2), accepted for use with the SI. Not the instantaneous Earth-Sun distance.
items.quote: astronomical unit (j)   au         1 au = 149 597 870 700 m
items.confidenceNotes: The IAU PDF itself could not be fetched (see excluded); the BIPM brochure is an authoritative secondary carrier of the same exact value.

items.labelEn: Light time for one astronomical unit
items.labelFr: Temps-lumière pour une unité astronomique
items.conditions: Vacuum, 1 au exactly; approximates Sun-Earth one-way light time (real distance varies over the year).
items.calculation: t = 149 597 870 700 m / 299 792 458 m/s; inputs: astronomical-unit, speed-of-light-vacuum
items.locator: Table 8 PDF p. 30; Table 1 PDF p. 14
items.confidenceNotes: About 8 min 19 s.

items.labelEn: Earth-Moon orbit semimajor axis
items.labelFr: Demi-grand axe de l'orbite lunaire
items.conditions: Semimajor axis (0.3844 x 10^6 km). low/high: the fact sheet's stated rough range of the actual Earth-Moon distance over a year (footnote).
items.locator: Orbital parameters table, row 'Semimajor axis (10^6 km)'; footnote to perigee/apogee
items.quote: Semimajor axis (106 km) | 0.3844
items.confidenceNotes: Range quote: 'the distance from the Moon to Earth roughly ranges from 357,000 km to 407,000 km'. Mean perigee 0.3633 and mean apogee 0.4055 x 10^6 km also listed. Semimajor axis is not strictly the time-averaged distance.

items.labelEn: Earth-Moon one-way light time (semimajor axis)
items.labelFr: Temps-lumière Terre-Lune, aller simple (demi-grand axe)
items.conditions: Vacuum, centre-to-centre distance equal to the semimajor axis; low/high from the 357,000-407,000 km range. Ignores ground-station and surface offsets.
items.calculation: t = 384 400 000 m / 299 792 458 m/s; low = 357e6/c; high = 407e6/c; inputs: earth-moon-semimajor-axis, speed-of-light-vacuum
items.quote: Semimajor axis (106 km) | 0.3844
items.confidenceNotes: Round trip = 2.5644 s. No primary Apollo communications document was consulted for a measured round-trip value.

items.labelEn: Minimum Earth-Mars distance
items.labelFr: Distance minimale Terre-Mars
items.conditions: Fact sheet 'Distance from Earth: Minimum (10^6 km) 54.6'. Close oppositions only; most oppositions are farther.
items.locator: Mars Observational Parameters, 'Distance from Earth', row 'Minimum (10^6 km)'
items.quote: Minimum (106 km) 54.6
items.confidenceNotes: Quote reconstructed from table cells label + value.

items.labelEn: Maximum Earth-Mars distance
items.labelFr: Distance maximale Terre-Mars
items.conditions: Near solar conjunction (radio links are then generally disrupted by the Sun).
items.locator: Mars Observational Parameters, 'Distance from Earth', row 'Maximum (10^6 km)'
items.quote: Maximum (106 km) 401.4
items.confidenceNotes: Quote reconstructed from table cells label + value.

items.labelEn: Earth-Mars one-way light time at minimum distance
items.labelFr: Temps-lumière Terre-Mars, aller simple, à la distance minimale
items.conditions: Vacuum, Earth-Mars distance 54.6e6 km (fact-sheet minimum); about 3.0 min.
items.calculation: t = 54.6e9 m / 299 792 458 m/s; inputs: earth-mars-distance-min, speed-of-light-vacuum
items.quote: Minimum (106 km) 54.6
items.confidenceNotes: NASA Goddard outreach page gives rounded 'about four minutes' and 'around 24 minutes'; its 24 min does not match its own 250 million miles (about 22.4 min), so the calculated range is preferred.

items.labelEn: Earth-Mars one-way light time at maximum distance
items.labelFr: Temps-lumière Terre-Mars, aller simple, à la distance maximale
items.conditions: Vacuum, Earth-Mars distance 401.4e6 km (fact-sheet maximum, near solar conjunction); about 22.3 min.
items.calculation: t = 401.4e9 m / 299 792 458 m/s; inputs: earth-mars-distance-max, speed-of-light-vacuum
items.quote: Maximum (106 km) 401.4
items.confidenceNotes: NASA Goddard outreach page gives rounded 'about four minutes' and 'around 24 minutes'; its 24 min does not match its own 250 million miles (about 22.4 min), so the calculated range is preferred.

items.labelEn: Voyager 1 distance from Earth (18 Nov 2026)
items.labelFr: Distance de Voyager 1 à la Terre (18 novembre 2026)
items.conditions: Snapshot dated Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, 2:16:07 a.m. PST. Increases continuously and oscillates with Earth's orbital motion.
items.quote: 16.094 billion miles (25.902 billion kilometers) away from Earth.
items.confidenceNotes: Must always be cited with its date. The page calls it about one light-day.

items.labelEn: Voyager 1 one-way light time (18 Nov 2026)
items.labelFr: Temps-lumière aller simple vers Voyager 1 (18 novembre 2026)
items.conditions: Vacuum, distance of 25.902e9 km on 2026-11-18 02:16:07 PST; about 24.0 h.
items.calculation: t = 25.902e12 m / 299 792 458 m/s; inputs: voyager1-distance-2026-11-18, speed-of-light-vacuum
items.quote: the distance light travels in 24 hours, also known as one light-day
items.confidenceNotes: Consistent with the page's own 'one light-day' statement. Precision limited to 5 significant figures by the distance.

items.labelEn: TCP initial retransmission timeout
items.labelFr: Délai initial de retransmission TCP (RTO)
items.conditions: Before any RTT measurement; SHOULD-level requirement of RFC 6298. Implementations may differ.
items.quote: the sender SHOULD set RTO <- 1 second
items.confidenceNotes: RFC 2988 previously used 3 s (see RFC 6298 Appendix A).

items.labelEn: TCP minimum retransmission timeout
items.labelFr: Délai minimal de retransmission TCP (RTO)
items.conditions: SHOULD-level rule of RFC 6298. Some widely used stacks use a lower minimum (not sourced here).
items.quote: Whenever RTO is computed, if it is less than 1 second, then the RTO SHOULD be rounded up to 1 second.
items.confidenceNotes: Normative recommendation, not a measurement of deployed behaviour.

items.labelEn: Lowest permitted cap on TCP RTO
items.labelFr: Plafond minimal autorisé pour le RTO TCP
items.conditions: An upper bound MAY be placed on RTO, provided it is at least 60 s.
items.quote: A maximum value MAY be placed on RTO provided it is at least 60 seconds.
items.confidenceNotes: It is a floor for the cap, not a typical value.

items.labelEn: TCP RTO after a SYN timeout
items.labelFr: RTO TCP après expiration d'un SYN
items.conditions: If the timer expired awaiting the ACK of a SYN and RTO < 3 s, RTO is reset to 3 s once data transmission begins.
items.quote: the RTO MUST be re-initialized to 3 seconds when data transmission begins
items.confidenceNotes: Backoff itself is doubling (rule 5.5).

items.labelEn: TCP Maximum Segment Lifetime (MSL)
items.labelFr: Durée de vie maximale d'un segment TCP (MSL)
items.conditions: Value assumed by the TCP specification; explicitly an engineering choice. TIME-WAIT lasts 2 MSL.
items.quote: For this specification the MSL is taken to be 2 minutes.
items.confidenceNotes: Same value as RFC 793 (1981). Implementations often use shorter TIME-WAIT (not sourced here).

items.labelEn: TCP initial sequence number clock tick
items.labelFr: Pas de l'horloge des numéros de séquence initiaux TCP
items.conditions: 32-bit counter that 'typically' increments at least once every roughly 4 us; not assumed realtime nor precise.
items.quote: This clock is a 32-bit counter that typically increments at least once every roughly 4 microseconds
items.confidenceNotes: Approximate by the source's own wording ('roughly').

items.labelEn: 5G NR URLLC user-plane latency target
items.labelFr: Objectif de latence plan usager 5G NR URLLC
items.conditions: Design target, one way, UL and DL each; L2/L3 SDU ingress to egress over the radio interface, no DRX; considered an average value. Analytical evaluation.
items.quote: For URLLC, the target for user plane latency should be 0.5ms for UL, and 0.5ms for DL.
items.confidenceNotes: Target, not a measured deployed latency.

items.labelEn: 5G NR URLLC reliability latency bound
items.labelFr: Latence associée à l'exigence de fiabilité 5G NR URLLC
items.conditions: Success probability 1-10^-5 for a 32-byte packet within 1 ms user-plane latency.
items.quote: A general URLLC reliability requirement for one transmission of a packet is 1-10-5 for 32 bytes with a user plane latency of 1ms.
items.confidenceNotes: Quote as extracted by pdftotext ('1-10-5' = 1-10^-5).

items.labelEn: 5G NR eMBB user-plane latency target
items.labelFr: Objectif de latence plan usager 5G NR eMBB
items.conditions: Design target, UL and DL each; same definition as 7.5.
items.quote: For eMBB, the target for user plane latency should be 4ms for UL, and 4ms for DL.
items.confidenceNotes: Target.

items.labelEn: Satellite (GEO) user-plane RTT target
items.labelFr: Objectif de RTT plan usager par satellite géostationnaire
items.conditions: Upper target when a GEO satellite link is involved; MEO up to 180 ms, LEO up to 50 ms in the same sentence.
items.quote: the target for user plane RTT can be as high as 600ms for GEO satellite systems
items.confidenceNotes: A target ceiling, not a measurement.

items.labelEn: Satellite (LEO) user-plane RTT target
items.labelFr: Objectif de RTT plan usager par satellite en orbite basse
items.conditions: Upper target for LEO satellite systems.
items.quote: up to 180ms for MEO satellite systems, and up to 50ms for LEO satellite systems.
items.confidenceNotes: Target ceiling.

items.labelEn: Minimum Ethernet frame size
items.labelFr: Taille minimale d'une trame Ethernet
items.conditions: Frame from destination address to FCS, excluding preamble and inter-frame gap.
items.locator: Section 9.1 'Frame sizes to be used on Ethernet'
items.quote: 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 1280, 1518 / These sizes include the maximum and minimum frame sizes permitted by the Ethernet standard
items.confidenceNotes: 64 as the minimum is inferred from the list including the minimum; IEEE 802.3 itself (minFrameSize) could not be consulted.

items.labelEn: Wire time of a minimum Ethernet frame at 1 Gbit/s (with preamble and gap)
items.labelFr: Durée d'occupation du lien par une trame Ethernet minimale à 1 Gbit/s (préambule et intervalle compris)
items.conditions: 64-byte frame + 64-bit preamble + 96-bit gap = 672 bits at a nominal 1e9 bit/s. Frame alone: 512 ns.
items.calculation: t = (64 bits preamble + 8 x 64 bits frame + 96 bits gap) / 1e9 bit/s = 672 bits / 1e9 bit/s; inputs: ethernet-min-frame-size, RFC 2544 Appendix B (preamble 64 bits, gap 96 bits)
items.quote: Preamble 64 bits / Frame 8 x N bits / Gap  96 bits
items.confidenceNotes: Cross-check: at 10 Mbit/s, 1/(672e-7 s) = 14 880.95 frames/s, matching RFC 2544 Appendix B '64 14880' for Ethernet. Line rate is a nominal parameter, not sourced from IEEE 802.3.

items.labelEn: Wire time of a minimum Ethernet frame at 10 Gbit/s (with preamble and gap)
items.labelFr: Durée d'occupation du lien par une trame Ethernet minimale à 10 Gbit/s (préambule et intervalle compris)
items.conditions: 672 bits at a nominal 1e10 bit/s. Frame alone: 51.2 ns.
items.calculation: t = 672 bits / 1e10 bit/s; inputs: ethernet-min-frame-size, RFC 2544 Appendix B (preamble 64 bits, gap 96 bits)
items.quote: Preamble 64 bits / Frame 8 x N bits / Gap  96 bits
items.confidenceNotes: Assumes the 10 Mbit/s-era preamble/gap structure carries over to 10GbE (true for the nominal minimum IPG but not checked against IEEE 802.3 clauses for 10G/100G).

items.labelEn: Wire time of a minimum Ethernet frame at 100 Gbit/s (with preamble and gap)
items.labelFr: Durée d'occupation du lien par une trame Ethernet minimale à 100 Gbit/s (préambule et intervalle compris)
items.conditions: 672 bits at a nominal 1e11 bit/s. Frame alone: 5.12 ns. Ignores 64b/66b line coding overhead.
items.calculation: t = 672 bits / 1e11 bit/s; inputs: ethernet-min-frame-size, RFC 2544 Appendix B
items.quote: Preamble 64 bits / Frame 8 x N bits / Gap  96 bits
items.confidenceNotes: Same caveat as the 10G item; 1 bit at 100 Gbit/s lasts 10 ps.

items.labelEn: Simple visual reaction time (mean, hardware-corrected)
items.labelFr: Temps de réaction simple visuel (moyenne, corrigée des délais matériels)
items.conditions: Community sample, n=1469, ages 18-65; lateralised visual stimuli, mouse-button press with dominant index finger; 231 ms uncorrected, 213 ms after subtracting measured display+mouse delay (averaged 17.8 ms).
items.quote: Mean SRT latencies were short (231, 213 ms when corrected for hardware delays)
items.confidenceNotes: Mean of subject means; Experiment 2 (n=189, ages 18-82, other lab) was about 7 ms slower. Latency rises with age.

items.labelEn: Visual stimulus detection time (SRT minus movement initiation)
items.labelFr: Temps de détection d'un stimulus visuel (TR simple moins initiation du mouvement)
items.conditions: Same sample (n=1469); estimated by subtracting finger-tapping movement-initiation time from SRT. Derived estimate, not directly observed.
items.quote: SDT latencies averaged 131 ms and were unaffected by age.
items.confidenceNotes: Model-dependent subtraction method.

items.labelEn: Duration of a voluntary eye blink
items.labelFr: Durée d'un clignement volontaire des yeux
items.conditions: Voluntary (not spontaneous) blinks; 25 healthy volunteers (11 M, 14 F), aged 25-63 (mean 35); high-speed video at 600 fps. Mean ± 25 ms (s.e. per Table 1 caption). Closing phase 76 ± 2 ms, closed 58 ± 4 ms.
items.quote: one voluntary blink took 572 ± 25 ms
items.confidenceNotes: Spontaneous blinks are generally reported as shorter, but no source for that was consulted here: do not use 572 ms as 'a blink' without the word 'voluntary'.

items.labelEn: Closing phase of a voluntary blink
items.labelFr: Phase de fermeture d'un clignement volontaire
items.conditions: Same study: n=25, 600 fps; mean ± 2 ms (s.e.).
items.quote: Closing phase: 76 ± 2 ms
items.confidenceNotes: Quote is the WebFetch rendering of a table cell (label + value), not a running-text sentence.

items.labelEn: Flicker fusion limit for uniform light
items.labelFr: Limite de fusion du papillotement en lumière uniforme
items.conditions: Spatially uniform modulated light; n=10 subjects; DLP projector setup. Sensitivity 'drops to zero near 65 Hz'.
items.quote: Sensitivity drops to zero near 65 Hz.
items.confidenceNotes: Small sample; 'near' is approximate. Classic CFF depends on luminance, eccentricity and contrast.

items.labelEn: Flicker artefact visibility with a spatial edge (median viewer)
items.labelFr: Visibilité des artefacts de papillotement avec un bord net (observateur médian)
items.conditions: Modulated light containing a high-spatial-frequency edge (eye movements across it); n=10; median viewer; several viewers above 800 Hz (high).
items.quote: For the median viewer, flicker artifacts disappear only over 500 Hz
items.confidenceNotes: n=10, two subjects are authors; single study, not replicated in the sources consulted. 'high' is a lower bound for some viewers, not a maximum.

items.labelEn: Just-noticeable stylus latency while dragging (large box, median)
items.labelFr: Latence de stylet juste perceptible en glisser (grande boîte, médiane)
items.conditions: n=16 naive adults (24-52 y); High Performance Stylus System with 1 ms baseline; JND by PEST adaptive procedure; task: dragging a stylus with a large box around the nib.
items.quote: Results ranged from 2 to 16 milliseconds, with a median latency of 6 milliseconds.
items.confidenceNotes: Internal inconsistency: the running text gives 'range 2 - 7' for the large box and '2 - 16' for the small box, opposite to the figure captions. Median values are consistent.

items.labelEn: Just-noticeable stylus latency while dragging (small box, median)
items.labelFr: Latence de stylet juste perceptible en glisser (petite boîte, médiane)
items.conditions: Same study, n=16; small box around the nib; 1 ms baseline.
items.quote: Results ranged from 2 to 7 milliseconds, with a median latency of 2 milliseconds.
items.confidenceNotes: Abstract: '~1 versus 2 milliseconds while dragging'. Same range inconsistency as above.

items.labelEn: Just-noticeable stylus latency while scribbling (median)
items.labelFr: Latence de stylet juste perceptible en gribouillage (médiane)
items.conditions: Same study, n=16; scribbling task with a 7 ms baseline latency.
items.quote: discriminate between the 7-millisecond baseline latency and a median of 40 milliseconds (Figure 11; range 10 - 70 milliseconds)
items.confidenceNotes: Quote joined across a line break in the PDF.
